lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: cleaning and laundry schedules

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic cleaning and laundry schedules task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: Before learning any new system, the learner looks back over the past two weeks and records, task by task, what cleaning and laundry work actually happened in their household and who did it, without judging or changing anything yet.
materials: learner-local: a calendar, planner, or phone calendar app to check dates from the past two weeks

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What is one thing this audit revealed about your current cleaning or laundry habits that you didn't expect to see written down?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g8-u02-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Audit thoroughness: Lists at least eight distinct tasks with frequency and who-did-it noted for each. | Honest self-assessment: Names a specific, plausible reason (habit, time, skill, someone else usually does it) for each of the six identified tasks. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner interview one other household member about their perception of the same two weeks, then compare the two records side by side and note any tasks where their accounts genuinely disagree.

resources.title: cleaning and laundry schedules worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Before learning any new system, the learner looks back over the past two weeks and records, task by task, what cleaning and laundry work actually happened in their household and who did it, without judging or changing anything yet.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact cleaning and laundry schedules decision or action.
Model move 2: Before recording specifics, take stock of your general sense of the household's cleaning rhythm.

Model move 3: Build a simple two-column list: on the left, write every cleaning or laundry task you can think of (dishes, vacuuming, wiping counters, sorting laundry, folding, trash, bathroom cleaning, and so on).

Model check: Audit thoroughness: Lists at least eight distinct tasks with frequency and who-did-it noted for each. | Honest self-assessment: Names a specific, plausible reason (habit, time, skill, someone else usually does it) for each of the six identified tasks.

resources.title: cleaning and laundry schedules action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for cleaning and laundry schedules.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: cleaning and laundry schedules coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Before learning any new system, the learner looks back over the past two weeks and records, task by task, what cleaning and laundry work actually happened in their household and who did it, without judging or changing anything yet.
Coach direction: Before recording specifics, take stock of your general sense of the household's cleaning rhythm.
Learner prompt: In one or two sentences, describe how cleaning and laundry currently get done in your household — is there a set schedule, or does it happen when something looks dirty?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: cleaning and laundry schedules complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Build a simple two-column list: on the left, write every cleaning or laundry task you can think of (dishes, vacuuming, wiping counters, sorting laundry, folding, trash, bathroom cleaning, and so on). On the right, mark how often each one actually happened in the past two weeks.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I listed at least eight distinct cleaning or laundry tasks that happen in my household.
Response 2 (t2-p2): For each task, I wrote how often it actually happened in the last two weeks (daily, a few times, once, or not at all).
Response 3 (t2-p3): For each task, I noted whether I did it myself, someone else did it, or it didn't get done.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: cleaning and laundry schedules minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What is one thing this audit revealed about your current cleaning or laundry habits that you didn't expect to see written down?

Success checks: Audit thoroughness: Lists at least eight distinct tasks with frequency and who-did-it noted for each. | Honest self-assessment: Names a specific, plausible reason (habit, time, skill, someone else usually does it) for each of the six identified tasks.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: cleaning and laundry schedules supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g8-u02-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional cleaning and laundry schedules condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Audit thoroughness: Lists at least eight distinct tasks with frequency and who-did-it noted for each. | Honest self-assessment: Names a specific, plausible reason (habit, time, skill, someone else usually does it) for each of the six identified tasks..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g8-u02-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
